applications.notes: Hi Bret, Thank you for checking directly. I want to be transparent: I have not worked hands-on inside Adobe Experience Platform, Real-Time CDP, AJO, CJA, Adobe Campaign, Adobe Target, AEM, Launch/Tags/Web SDK, or Adobe Query Service. However, I am a quick learner and I guarantee you, I will be matching foot to foot in no time joining the team. At TCS, I worked on the Equifax client account building Python, SQL, GCP, and Airflow pipelines for regulated credit-data workflows processing 10M+ records daily. applications.latestSubject: The silence isn't feedback
applications.notes: Hey Tirth, I want to talk about the silence. If you've sent applications and heard nothing back - no rejection, no acknowledgment, just nothing - I know what that can start to feel like. Like the market is telling you something about your worth. Like you're being passed over for a reason nobody will say out loud. I've been there. Eight hundred applications. Weeks of silence. And the silence is the worst part, because your brain fills it with explanations that almost always land in the wrong place. Here's what the silence actually means in most cases: Your application entered a queue with 300 others. The ATS filtered it. Or a recruiter spent six seconds on it during a Tuesday afternoon when they had forty more to get through. The decision wasn't careful. It wasn't personal. It was volume. The hiring process wasn't designed to find the best candidate. It was designed to efficiently reduce 400 applications to 15. Most of the filtering happens before anyone with context about the role has looked at your name. That's not an excuse for the system. It's just useful to know - because it means the silence is information about the process, not information about you. Next time I want to talk about what this process is actually costing you - beyond the rejections. — Leela Co-founder, Scale.jobs _We apply. applications.notes: If you’ve ever gone weeks or even months without a nibble on your job-hunt… It’s easy to beat yourself up thinking, “No-one wants to hire me!” But here’s the thing: The problem _ISN’T_ that employers hate your resume… It’s that they don’t read it in the first place! You see, employers have a technology that - if not taken into account - will end your chances in the hiring process before it’s even begun. What is this technology? It’s called an Applicant Tracking System (ATS), and it tests your resume on 2 basic things: Test #1: _Can I scan this resume?_ (If it can’t, because your resume uses a weird format, it likely won't get very far.) And Test #2: _How relevant is this resume to the job description?_ If the ATS gives you a poor relevance score, your resume gets kicked to the bottom of the candidate pile, where a hiring manager will click “reject” - without even reading it. (According to Harvard Business School, 88% of candidates are rejected like this) _“But Rohan, even with a low score, a hiring manager can still read my resume, right?”_ Well.. It’s a bit like asking “Could you read a website on page 18 of Google?” Yeah, you can… …but will you? So a better question to ask is… How do you make sure your resume is scannable by the ATS, and ranked high enough so it actually gets read by a human being? Well, for scannability.. If Score My Resume can read it, the ATS can too! And as for being ranked high enough… All you need to do is weave in enough keywords to let the ATS know you’re not a fisherman applying for a forensics job. applications.latestSubject: Vela technical follow-up - Tirth Shah
applications.notes: Hi Zorawar, Thank you for taking the time to go deep on the technical side today. I appreciated the questions around RAG architecture, ETL design, permission-based querying, API boundaries, and what I have broken, debugged, and rebuilt in past projects. The main reason Vela interests me is that the product sits at the exact intersection where I have been building: **data, energy, and AI**. Vela is not just adding a chat layer on top of project documents; it is turning fragmented infrastructure data into a live operating model that can trace changes, identify downstream impact, cite sources, route work, and stage actions behind human approval. From a technical perspective, this is how I would think about contributing: - I would start with the project model first: organizations, companies, projects, memberships, documents, source records, extracted events, impacted objects, recommendations, approvals, and audit logs. - I would treat every connector and API as a contract across authentication, authorization, schema, validation, idempotency, retries, error handling, and auditability. - I would design the RAG layer around permission-aware retrieval, source metadata, citations, and evaluation, not just embeddings and prompt quality. - I would separate recommendation from execution so Vela can draft, stage, and route actions while keeping final writeback behind scoped permissions and named approval. - I would keep the first product slice narrow, such as a source change that becomes an extracted event, maps to an impacted milestone/register field, and appears as a reviewable PM card with citations. My background maps to that work in a practical way. At Texas A&M Utilities, I built Python and SQL Server workflows across ERCOT, weather, solar, billing, CHP, thermal-storage, and sensor data with validation gates, retries, logs, alerts, and operator handoff. At Mays, I built a 29.6K-line analytics and AI platform with a 17-table warehouse, LangChain/OpenRouter assistant, schema RAG, SQL tools, OAuth/RBAC, and context management. At Black Tie, I helped ship a zero-to-one Next.js, TypeScript, Tailwind, Supabase/Postgres, Stripe, Maps, APIs, and webhook-based product from founder requirements to live usage in 12 weeks. I also want to be clear about how I work. I do not pretend to know every EPC or interconnection workflow yet, and I would not overstate my HCLTech work as live Verizon network automation. Where I do not know the domain detail, I will sit with users, read the actual artifacts, ask direct questions, and build the smallest useful version that proves the workflow. That is the attitude I would bring as a founding engineer: learn fast, build carefully, and own the messy last mile. On the practical side, I can start quickly and I am open to relocating to San Francisco for the right founding role. Beyond housing, food, and travel logistics, what would help me contribute fastest is early access to the product context, a clear first 30-day problem, custome

applications.latestSubject: Thank You for Applying to DailyPay
applications.notes: Hi Tirth, We have received your application for the Data Engineer II opportunity. Thank you for your application! We’re building a new financial system that starts working, the minute work starts. Each of us believes that the long-term success of our company is 100% dependent on the success of our people — a collection of high-performing individuals who bring diverse experiences, perspectives, and backgrounds to carry out our mission. DailyPay provides an industry-leading earned wage access platform that gives employees access to their pay when they want it. DailyPay’s platform boosts employee financial wellness and keeps them more engaged, motivated and happier at work. For employers, this translates to improved retention and increased productivity. Our Process At DailyPay, we believe no one should have to spend countless hours interviewing. A typical interview process includes an introductory call with a Talent Partner, time spent with the Hiring Manager, and opportunity to meet with members of the team, and in some instances, a presentation. DailyPay Talent Partners review every incoming resume and aim to respond within a few days of your application. Due to the high volume of applications we receive, it may take more than 72 hours to respond. If you are selected for an initial interview, a Talent Partner will reach out to you to schedule time to connect. applications.latestSubject: AI-native professional with AWS expertise- San Jose (California) or RTP (North Carolina)- 12+ month Contract
applications.notes: Hi Tirth , I hope you're doing well. My name is Harshit Singh , and I'm a Sr. Recruiter with ClifyX Inc. I came across your profile and believe your experience aligns well with an exciting opportunity we're currently hiring for below role.If you're interested, please send me your updated resume along with your work authorization, current location, expected rate, and availability. Happy to share more details once I hear from you. Job Title: AI-native professional with AWS expertise Location: San Jose (California) or RTP (North Carolina) Duration: 12+ month Contract JOB DESCRIPTION: Looking for Visa independent only (NO 1099 AND EAD) Who You Are You've made the shift from being an experienced, effective software engineer to being an AI-native one: • You have proven experience serving as a software engineer for web application projects, hosted On-Premise and Cloud, supporting a large customer base. • You treat performance as a design constraint, not a tuning pass after the fact. • You know when to build and when to reach for a managed AWS service — you can justify that trade-off based on the problem. • You think in systems and evaluate designs critically — whether reviewing AI-generated code or your own architecture — catching the subtle bug, security gap, or design choice that won't hold up under load or misuse. • You use spec-driven development with AI as your default way of engineering software. • You pick up new tools and approaches quickly, since the effective way to work with AI changes often, and you'd rather adapt early than fall behind. • You are decisive without being divisive — you can analytically weigh trade-offs, balance competing priorities, and drive decisions that span organizational boundaries. • You have excellent communication and organization skills. Minimum Qualifications • BS or MS degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or a related technical field, or demonstrated equivalent experience. • Demonstrated fluency in leveraging AI technologies across the entire software development lifecycle, including breaking down user stories into actionable tasks, AI-assisted coding and testing, automated defect resolution, and deployment of fully tested software. • Deep, hands-on experience building and deploying production systems on AWS (e.g., EC2,Lambda, ECS/EKS, S3, RDS/DynamoDB, API Gateway), with a track record of real, customer-facing applications running in production. • Server-side software development experience with Python, Java, NodeJS, and/or other similar technologies; client-side web application development experience using React, Backbone, native JavaScript, and/or other comparable technologies. Expertise in building secure, large-scale systems using fault-tolerant technologies (such as Elasticsearch, Cockroach DB, Oracle, MongoDB & Kafka). Thanks & Warm Regards, Harshit Singh (Sr. Recruiter) Cell: (908) 293-8259 Headquarters: South

applications.latestSubject: Job open :: AI Engineer  :: Remote 100% - Canada ::
applications.notes: 08/27/26 5:53 PM Dear Tirth, My name is Alex and I'm an IT recruiter at Epsilon Solutions. Our records show that you are an experienced IT professional with experience in AI . This experience is relevant to one of my current openings. Title: AI Engineer Location: Remote 100% - Canada. Terms: 12+ months Job Overview Senior‑level role on a five‑person engineering team building a production‑grade healthcare conversational GenAI platform. The stack centers on Python 3.12+ , FastAPI , and Google ADK 2.0 as the primary multi‑agent orchestration and structured‑output toolkit, deployed on Azure . The role emphasizes backend service development, GenAI workflow engineering, secure integrations, and operational ownership for patient‑facing conversational experiences. Key Responsibilities Design, implement, and maintain backend APIs and services using Python 3.12+ and FastAPI. Develop and operate multi‑agent GenAI workflows using Google ADK 2.0 as the primary orchestration framework. Integrate and tune LLM providers and GenAI toolkits (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google). Support and extend workflows built with other orchestration frameworks (LangGraph, LangChain, PydanticAI) and ensure interoperability. Implement RAG, prompt engineering, structured output validation, and AI guardrails to ensure safe, reliable model behavior. Build domain task handlers for healthcare workflows (care tasks, medications, scheduling) and integrate with clinical systems as required. Leverage Azure services (Cosmos DB, App Configuration, Key Vault, Event Hubs, Application Insights) for data, configuration, secrets, and telemetry. Ensure API security and PHI protection using JWT/OAuth and security best practices. Contribute to architecture, code reviews, production support, observability, and incident response. Author and maintain automated tests (pytest) and support CI/CD and containerized deployments. Required Qualifications professional software development experience. Strong production experience in Python and asynchronous frameworks ( FastAPI preferred). Hands‑on experience with Google ADK 2.0 for multi‑agent orchestration and structured LLM outputs. Familiarity with other LLM orchestration frameworks (LangGraph, LangChain, PydanticAI) and ability to work across toolchains. Demonstrated knowledge of prompt engineering , RAG , structured output validation, and AI safety/guardrail patterns. Experience integrating OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and Google ADK 2.0 . Practical experience with Azure services (Cosmos DB, Key Vault, App Configuration). Familiarity with Docker , CI/CD (e.g., GitHub Actions), and containerized production deployments. Experience with event‑driven architectures and workflow engines. Strong understanding of JWT/OAuth and API security best practices. Proven ability to operate with high ownership in a small, fast‑paced team. Thanks and Regards, Alex S Technical Recruiter P: 6479058191 /+1 (669) -699-0890 E: alex.s@epsilonsolutions.ca Epsilon solutions http://epsilonsolu

Job Description: The client team is developing a central data warehouse called the ISIM-B Program (Integrated Service Information and Management “B” Division) with the goal of building analytics that aims to improve the passenger experience for riders by pursuing and addressing various elements of the subway system. The Data Warehouse is intended to provide NYCT with information about the effectiveness, timeliness and quality of the various services that NYCT delivers and to provide operational insights to management at various levels. This position will be responsible for developing data pipelines to move data between source and target systems. (Extracting data from the source systems and transforming/loading it into the Data Warehouse, which is our target). applications.notes: Dear Harsh Razz , I hope you’re doing well. My name is Tirth Shah , and I’m a Data Engineer with over four years of experience building scalable data pipelines, cloud data platforms, data warehouses, and analytics-ready datasets. applications.latestSubject: N26: Thank you for applying to Data Engineer - Platform Engineering!
applications.notes: Hi Tirth, Thanks for applying to help us build N26, the bank the world loves to use! We know applying for a job can be exciting, and at times nerve-racking. To provide you some visibility, here's a rundown on our hiring process: Application Review 📜 and Timing ⏳ All of our applications are reviewed by humans - not robots. Due to the volume of applications we receive, reviewing all profiles and providing feedback to each candidate proves to be time-consuming. We aim to get back to applicants within 1 week. Generally we’re pretty good at this, but sometimes it can run a bit longer. We've been there too, so for that reason we’ll do our best to keep the wait to a minimum. Interview Process 🤝 If unfortunately you don’t make it past the CV review, it means that currently you do not meet the requirements for the specific role (for now). If it seems like a good fit, then we’ll reach out to you. In general you can expect a series of digital meetings with different team members paired with a practical challenge. The full interview cycle usually averages between 2 to 4 weeks, but this might vary based on seniority of the role and agenda availability. Successful applicants will be asked to submit professional references and complete a criminal record check. We'll share more details about this when you reach this stage in our hiring process. In the meantime, check out more on what life could be like with us on our LinkedIn ( https://www.linkedin.com/company/n26/ ) page, our N26 Blog ( https://n26.com/en-eu/blog/category/insiden26 ) and our People of N26 Instagram ( https://www.instagram.com/peopleofn26/ ) profile. Thanks again for your interest in building the bank the world loves to use! Best regards, Your N26 Recruitment Team

applications.latestSubject: Data Architect/Engineer | Deerfield Beach, FL
applications.notes: Hello Tirth, I am Prabhat Kumar, a recruiter with Pyramid Consulting, Inc. a leading staffing organization. I came across your profile in one of the job boards and feel that your skills and professional experience would be a good fit for a position with one of our premier clients. Please review the job description below. If you are interested in this position please forward your updated resume for immediate consideration and preferred time to discuss this opportunity further. Title: Data Architect/Engineer Location: FL; Deerfield Beach (Fully Onsite) [OEPN TO RE-LOCATE WILL WORK] Duration: 06-12 Months (Contract to Potential Hire) PR Range: $55 - $60/hr. Employee benefits include, but are not limited to, health insurance (medical, dental, vision), 401(k) plan, and paid sick leave (depending on work location). Job Description: The Data Architect will have end-to-end vision to see how a logical design will translate into one or more physical Databases, and how the Data will flow through the successive Stages involved. The incumbent will need to be able to address issues of Data Migration (Validation, Clean-up and Mapping), and will need to understand the importance of Data Dictionaries. This individual will also be responsible for providing technical leadership for projects and will be accountable for the end-to-end solution delivery. Additionally, this individual will be the focal and escalation point for all technical and technical delivery issues on the effort. A data architect will be involved in data governance practices, in data administration, in data integration, and in data modeling. Data architect will be the one establishing policies and goals for those areas. Data Architects will be the one building the conceptual architecture for Data Governance, administration, integration, and modeling. The data architect will be the primary accountable person for the design and delivery of the data solution for the business initiative. Technical Requirements Minimum of 10 years of experience as a Data Architect Extensive knowledge of data warehouse and BI techniques In depth hands on working experience with Azure SQL, Synapse and ADF Data Pipelines to ingest data from Azure (such as SQL, Cosmos, ADLS Gen 2.0) and non-Azure sources to Synapse Working knowledge of Azure Devops CI/CD pipelines to promote Synapse Databases and Data pipelines from non-production to production environments. In depth hands on working experience of Data modeling and Database Design In depth hands on working experience of SQL, NoSQL and Big Data knowledge In depth understanding of Azure Database Security Particularly Encryption, Obfuscation, Role based Access control, etc. Strong analytical and problem solving skills Tools knowledge for Data Disciplines A background in computer science and database management. Architecture Responsibilities: Participate in Data Governance meeting to provide guidance and advocate how we can help the business be more successful, including participation with Data Management organizations to Define ownership, usage, security and quality for all data Works directly with Data Analysts, Solution Architects and Vendors to understand and validate requirements and translate business requirements into technical requirements and designs Develops strategies for data acquisitions, archive recovery, and implementation of a database. Logical design of Databases, Data Warehouses and Multidimensional Databases including data flows, conception model and logical models Serving as a consulting resource for Delivery and Support Creating strategy and recommendations on a company s future data and tech policies Collaborating with other team members to build the ideal database, data integration and business intelligence infrastructure and platforms Establish Data Architecture Design Patterns and best practices Forward thinking on new technologies and patterns Technology strategy and roadmaps Thanks and Regards, Prabhat Kumar Patro Recruiter Pyram

Cross-Functional Coordination Coordinate activities across Development, QA, Business, DevOps, Infrastructure, and Vendor teams. Manage cross-POD dependencies, action tracking, and issue escalations. Ensure alignment between business priorities and technical execution timelines. Support global delivery coordination across offshore/onshore teams. Stakeholder Communication & Reporting Provide regular status updates to leadership and business stakeholders. Drive governance meetings, operational reviews, deployment reviews, and escalation calls. Maintain project dashboards, risk registers, release trackers, and support metrics. Enable GenAI-based reporting and operational dashboard automation where applicable. Required Skills & Experience Mandatory 10+ years of IT project management experience. Experience managing PLM implementation, support, or enhancement projects. Strong experience coordinating global cross-functional teams. Experience managing production support, release management, and deployment governance. Preferred Exposure to Teamcenter modules including Item, BOM, Change Management, CAD/xCAD, Reports, and Integrations. Experience supporting highly customized enterprise applications. Familiarity with SAP integrations, DevOps processes, and enterprise deployment models. Exposure to GenAI-enabled reporting or PMO automation initiatives. This includes comparing your submission with consideration to the role summary and requirements. - If a member of the HR team or Manager determines that you meet or exceed the requirements you may be contacted for a phone or video interview. If you are not selected for additional consideration we encourage you to continue visiting our career site as new opportunities are posted on a daily basis. - If the interview goes well, you may be asked to complete an additional interview, possibly in person. This may include the Manager or other members of the team. - If you are selected as the final candidate a member of the HR team will work with you and the Manager to prepare an offer of employment. applications.latestSubject: Thank you for applying to Redwood Materials
applications.notes: Hi Tirth, Thank you for your interest in Redwood Materials! Your email has been received and we're excited that you would consider joining our team. Redwood’s goal is to develop and deploy new technologies for dramatically increasing the scope and scale of recycled and sustainable materials in global supply chains. We’re passionate about building a sustainable future and changing the world with a small team. With that said, we’re thrilled that you’re excited about helping us solve this super important and difficult environmental problem. We will review your information as soon as we can and we'll be in touch if your qualifications align with our needs. Due to the volume of emails received, we want to be respectful of your time and let you know that we will only be reaching out to candidates whose skillsets best match our roles. If our team feels that you’re a fit, we will contact you shortly about next steps. If you don’t hear back immediately, don't worry! We're growing fast and will have new roles opening up in the future, so please keep an eye on our website for updates! Recycle with Us Redwood’s focus is to take both end-of-life electric vehicle batteries and other lithium-ion powered consumer devices and then recycle, refine, and remanufacture them into new products here in America. The largest lithium and cobalt mines in the western hemisphere can be found in the junk drawers of America and we’re on a mission to collect as many of these old products as possible. We encourage all candidates, visitors, and guests to bring old phones, laptops, tablets, electric toothbrushes, and any other rechargeable device with a lithium-ion battery. For more information about our consumer recycling program, please visit our website ( https://www.redwoodmaterials.com/recyclewithus ). Thanks, Redwood Recruiting

The technical skills interview will focus on the skills and knowledge you have put forward in your application. The final interview focuses on behavioural questions based on your previous employment or academic experience. You will also be asked situational questions which will relate to the role for which you are applying to see how you can fit in with what we're trying to achieve. Due to the volume of applications we receive please be aware that you may not receive a personal response beyond this. Incomplete applications such as those which did not answer questions or complete testing are severely disadvantaged. Thank you again for taking the time to apply - we'll be in touch if you are selected to move forward.
